# C# Classes Crash Course

Let me walk you through C# classes with practical examples!

## Basic Class Structure & Initialization


A class is a blueprint for creating objects. Here's the fundamental structure:

```csharp
public class Person
{
    // Fields (private data)
    private string name;
    private int age;
    
    // Constructor
    public Person(string name, int age)
    {
        this.name = name;
        this.age = age;
    }
    
    // Method
    public void Introduce()
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"Hi, I'm {name} and I'm {age} years old.");
    }
}

// Usage
var person = new Person("Alice", 30);
person.Introduce();
// Output: Hi, I'm Alice and I'm 30 years old.
```

**Key Points:**
- Fields store object data
- Constructor initializes the object when created with `new`
- `this` keyword refers to the current instance


## Multiple Constructors


C# supports constructor overloading - multiple constructors with different parameters:

```csharp
public class Book
{
    private string title;
    private string author;
    private int pages;
    
    // Constructor 1: All parameters
    public Book(string title, string author, int pages)
    {
        this.title = title;
        this.author = author;
        this.pages = pages;
    }
    
    // Constructor 2: Title and author only
    public Book(string title, string author)
    {
        this.title = title;
        this.author = author;
        this.pages = 0; // Default value
    }
    
    // Constructor 3: Title only
    public Book(string title)
    {
        this.title = title;
        this.author = "Unknown";
        this.pages = 0;
    }
    
    public void Display()
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{title} by {author} ({pages} pages)");
    }
}

// Usage
var book1 = new Book("1984", "George Orwell", 328);
var book2 = new Book("Animal Farm", "George Orwell");
var book3 = new Book("Untitled");

book1.Display(); // 1984 by George Orwell (328 pages)
book2.Display(); // Animal Farm by George Orwell (0 pages)
book3.Display(); // Untitled by Unknown (0 pages)
```

**Constructor Chaining:**

You can call one constructor from another using `: this()`:

```csharp
public class Book
{
    private string title;
    private string author;
    private int pages;
    
    // Main constructor
    public Book(string title, string author, int pages)
    {
        this.title = title;
        this.author = author;
        this.pages = pages;
    }
    
    // Delegates to main constructor
    public Book(string title, string author) : this(title, author, 0)
    {
    }
    
    // Delegates to previous constructor
    public Book(string title) : this(title, "Unknown")
    {
    }
}
```


## Instance vs Static Members


```
Instance Members              Static Members
----------------              --------------
   [Object 1]                    [Class]
   - field1                   - staticField
   - field2                   + StaticMethod()
   + Method()                    (shared by all)
                             
   [Object 2]
   - field1
   - field2
   + Method()

Each object has              Belongs to the class
its own copy                 itself, not instances
```

**Example:**

```csharp
public class Counter
{
    // Instance field - each object has its own
    private int instanceCount;
    
    // Static field - shared across all instances
    private static int totalCount = 0;
    
    // Constructor
    public Counter()
    {
        instanceCount = 0;
        totalCount++; // Increment shared counter
    }
    
    // Instance method
    public void Increment()
    {
        instanceCount++;
    }
    
    // Instance method
    public int GetInstanceCount()
    {
        return instanceCount;
    }
    
    // Static method - can be called without creating an object
    public static int GetTotalCount()
    {
        return totalCount;
    }
}

// Usage
var counter1 = new Counter();
counter1.Increment();
counter1.Increment();

var counter2 = new Counter();
counter2.Increment();

Console.WriteLine($"Counter 1: {counter1.GetInstanceCount()}"); // 2
Console.WriteLine($"Counter 2: {counter2.GetInstanceCount()}"); // 1
Console.WriteLine($"Total counters: {Counter.GetTotalCount()}"); // 2
```

**Key Differences:**
- **Instance members:** Accessed through object instances (`counter1.Increment()`)
- **Static members:** Accessed through class name (`Counter.GetTotalCount()`)
- Static members cannot access instance members directly


## Access Modifiers


Access modifiers control who can see and use your class members:

```
+-----------+---------------+-----------+-----------+-----------+
| Modifier  | Same Class    | Derived   | Same      | Different |
|           |               | Class     | Assembly  | Assembly  |
+-----------+---------------+-----------+-----------+-----------+
| public    |      ✓        |     ✓     |     ✓     |     ✓     |
| protected |      ✓        |     ✓     |     ✗     |     ✗     |
| internal  |      ✓        |     ✓     |     ✓     |     ✗     |
| private   |      ✓        |     ✗     |     ✗     |     ✗     |
+-----------+---------------+-----------+-----------+-----------+
```

**Example:**

```csharp
public class BankAccount
{
    // Private: Only accessible within this class
    private decimal balance;
    
    // Public: Accessible from anywhere
    public string AccountNumber { get; set; }
    
    // Protected: Accessible in this class and derived classes
    protected decimal interestRate;
    
    // Internal: Accessible within the same assembly
    internal string BankCode { get; set; }
    
    public BankAccount(string accountNumber, decimal initialBalance)
    {
        AccountNumber = accountNumber;
        balance = initialBalance;
        interestRate = 0.02m;
    }
    
    // Public method to access private field
    public decimal GetBalance()
    {
        return balance;
    }
    
    public void Deposit(decimal amount)
    {
        if (amount > 0)
            balance += amount;
    }
}

// Usage
var account = new BankAccount("123456", 1000m);
Console.WriteLine(account.AccountNumber); // ✓ OK - public
// Console.WriteLine(account.balance);    // ✗ Error - private
Console.WriteLine(account.GetBalance());  // ✓ OK - via public method
```


## Getters and Setters


### Traditional Getter/Setter Methods


```csharp
public class Rectangle
{
    private double width;
    private double height;
    
    // Getter
    public double GetWidth()
    {
        return width;
    }
    
    // Setter with validation
    public void SetWidth(double value)
    {
        if (value > 0)
            width = value;
        else
            throw new ArgumentException("Width must be positive");
    }
    
    public double GetHeight()
    {
        return height;
    }
    
    public void SetHeight(double value)
    {
        if (value > 0)
            height = value;
        else
            throw new ArgumentException("Height must be positive");
    }
}
```

### Auto-Properties (Recommended)


Modern C# way - compiler generates backing field automatically:

```csharp
public class Product
{
    // Auto-property (get and set)
    public string Name { get; set; }
    
    // Auto-property with private setter
    public decimal Price { get; private set; }
    
    // Auto-property with default value
    public int Stock { get; set; } = 0;
    
    // Read-only auto-property (can only be set in constructor)
    public string Id { get; }
    
    public Product(string id, string name, decimal price)
    {
        Id = id;  // OK - can set in constructor
        Name = name;
        Price = price;
    }
    
    public void UpdatePrice(decimal newPrice)
    {
        if (newPrice > 0)
            Price = newPrice;
    }
}

// Usage
var product = new Product("P001", "Laptop", 999.99m);
product.Name = "Gaming Laptop";  // OK - public setter
// product.Price = 800;          // Error - private setter
product.UpdatePrice(899.99m);    // OK - via method
```

### Computed Properties (Expression-bodied)


Properties that calculate values on-the-fly:

```csharp
public class Circle
{
    public double Radius { get; set; }
    
    // Computed property - no backing field
    public double Diameter => Radius * 2;
    
    public double Area => Math.PI * Radius * Radius;
    
    public double Circumference => 2 * Math.PI * Radius;
    
    // Can also have logic in get block
    public string Size
    {
        get
        {
            if (Radius < 5) return "Small";
            if (Radius < 10) return "Medium";
            return "Large";
        }
    }
}

// Usage
var circle = new Circle { Radius = 5 };
Console.WriteLine($"Radius: {circle.Radius}");
Console.WriteLine($"Diameter: {circle.Diameter}");
Console.WriteLine($"Area: {circle.Area:F2}");
Console.WriteLine($"Size: {circle.Size}");
```

**Property Comparison:**

```csharp
public class Employee
{
    // Backing field
    private string _fullName;
    
    // 1. Full property (manual control)
    public string FullName
    {
        get { return _fullName; }
        set { _fullName = value?.Trim(); }
    }
    
    // 2. Auto-property (simple, no logic)
    public string Email { get; set; }
    
    // 3. Computed property (read-only, calculated)
    public string DisplayName => $"{FullName} ({Email})";
    
    // 4. Init-only property (set once during initialization)
    public string EmployeeId { get; init; }
}
```


## Inheritance


```
       [Animal]
      /    |    \
     /     |     \
  [Dog] [Cat] [Bird]
```

Inheritance creates an "is-a" relationship:

```csharp
// Base class
public class Animal
{
    public string Name { get; set; }
    protected int age;
    
    public Animal(string name, int age)
    {
        Name = name;
        this.age = age;
    }
    
    // Virtual method - can be overridden
    public virtual void MakeSound()
    {
        Console.WriteLine("Some generic animal sound");
    }
    
    public void Sleep()
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{Name} is sleeping...");
    }
}

// Derived class
public class Dog : Animal
{
    public string Breed { get; set; }
    
    // Call base constructor with : base()
    public Dog(string name, int age, string breed) : base(name, age)
    {
        Breed = breed;
    }
    
    // Override base method
    public override void MakeSound()
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{Name} says: Woof! Woof!");
    }
    
    // New method specific to Dog
    public void Fetch()
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{Name} is fetching the ball!");
    }
}

public class Cat : Animal
{
    public Cat(string name, int age) : base(name, age)
    {
    }
    
    public override void MakeSound()
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{Name} says: Meow!");
    }
    
    public void Scratch()
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{Name} is scratching the furniture!");
    }
}

// Usage
Animal animal = new Animal("Generic", 5);
Dog dog = new Dog("Buddy", 3, "Golden Retriever");
Cat cat = new Cat("Whiskers", 2);

animal.MakeSound(); // Some generic animal sound
dog.MakeSound();    // Buddy says: Woof! Woof!
cat.MakeSound();    // Whiskers says: Meow!

dog.Fetch();        // Buddy is fetching the ball!
cat.Scratch();      // Whiskers is scratching the furniture!

// Polymorphism - treating derived classes as base class
Animal[] animals = { animal, dog, cat };
foreach (var a in animals)
{
    a.MakeSound();  // Calls appropriate overridden method
    a.Sleep();      // Inherited method
}
```

**Key Inheritance Keywords:**
- `virtual`: Method can be overridden in derived classes
- `override`: Overrides a virtual method from base class
- `base`: Access base class members
- `sealed`: Prevents further inheritance


## Interfaces & Abstract Classes


### Interfaces


An interface is a contract - defines WHAT a class must do, not HOW:

```csharp
// Interface - only method signatures, no implementation
public interface IPlayable
{
    void Play();
    void Pause();
    void Stop();
}

public interface IRecordable
{
    void StartRecording();
    void StopRecording();
}

// Class can implement multiple interfaces
public class MusicPlayer : IPlayable
{
    private bool isPlaying;
    
    public void Play()
    {
        isPlaying = true;
        Console.WriteLine("Music is playing...");
    }
    
    public void Pause()
    {
        Console.WriteLine("Music paused");
    }
    
    public void Stop()
    {
        isPlaying = false;
        Console.WriteLine("Music stopped");
    }
}

// Implementing multiple interfaces
public class VoiceRecorder : IPlayable, IRecordable
{
    public void Play()
    {
        Console.WriteLine("Playing recording...");
    }
    
    public void Pause()
    {
        Console.WriteLine("Playback paused");
    }
    
    public void Stop()
    {
        Console.WriteLine("Playback stopped");
    }
    
    public void StartRecording()
    {
        Console.WriteLine("Recording started...");
    }
    
    public void StopRecording()
    {
        Console.WriteLine("Recording stopped");
    }
}

// Usage with polymorphism
IPlayable player1 = new MusicPlayer();
IPlayable player2 = new VoiceRecorder();

player1.Play();
player2.Play();
```

### Abstract Classes


An abstract class is a partial implementation - defines both WHAT and some HOW:

```csharp
// Abstract class - cannot be instantiated directly
public abstract class Shape
{
    // Normal property
    public string Color { get; set; }
    
    // Abstract method - must be implemented by derived classes
    public abstract double CalculateArea();
    
    // Abstract method
    public abstract double CalculatePerimeter();
    
    // Concrete method - shared implementation
    public void Display()
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"Shape: {GetType().Name}");
        Console.WriteLine($"Color: {Color}");
        Console.WriteLine($"Area: {CalculateArea():F2}");
        Console.WriteLine($"Perimeter: {CalculatePerimeter():F2}");
    }
}

public class Circle : Shape
{
    public double Radius { get; set; }
    
    public Circle(double radius, string color)
    {
        Radius = radius;
        Color = color;
    }
    
    public override double CalculateArea()
    {
        return Math.PI * Radius * Radius;
    }
    
    public override double CalculatePerimeter()
    {
        return 2 * Math.PI * Radius;
    }
}

public class Rectangle : Shape
{
    public double Width { get; set; }
    public double Height { get; set; }
    
    public Rectangle(double width, double height, string color)
    {
        Width = width;
        Height = height;
        Color = color;
    }
    
    public override double CalculateArea()
    {
        return Width * Height;
    }
    
    public override double CalculatePerimeter()
    {
        return 2 * (Width + Height);
    }
}

// Usage
// Shape shape = new Shape(); // Error - cannot instantiate abstract class

Shape circle = new Circle(5, "Red");
Shape rectangle = new Rectangle(4, 6, "Blue");

circle.Display();
Console.WriteLine();
rectangle.Display();
```

### When to Use What?


```
Interface                Abstract Class              Concrete Class
---------                --------------              --------------
- Pure contract          - Partial implementation    - Full implementation
- No implementation      - Can have concrete         - No abstract members
- Multiple inheritance   - Single inheritance        - Can be instantiated
- "can do" relationship  - "is a" relationship       - Regular class

Examples:                Examples:                   Examples:
IPlayable                Shape                       Circle
IComparable              Vehicle                     Rectangle
IDisposable              Database                    SqlDatabase
```

**Example combining both:**

```csharp
// Interface
public interface IVehicle
{
    void Start();
    void Stop();
}

// Abstract class implementing interface
public abstract class Vehicle : IVehicle
{
    public string Brand { get; set; }
    public int Year { get; set; }
    
    // Abstract method
    public abstract void Drive();
    
    // Interface implementation
    public virtual void Start()
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{Brand} starting...");
    }
    
    public virtual void Stop()
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{Brand} stopping...");
    }
}

// Concrete class
public class Car : Vehicle
{
    public int Doors { get; set; }
    
    public override void Drive()
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{Brand} car is driving on the road");
    }
}

public class Motorcycle : Vehicle
{
    public bool HasSidecar { get; set; }
    
    public override void Drive()
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{Brand} motorcycle is cruising");
    }
    
    // Override interface method with custom behavior
    public override void Start()
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{Brand} motorcycle: Vroom vroom!");
    }
}
```


## Quick Reference Table

```
+------------------+------------------------------------------+
| Feature          | Use Case                                 |
+------------------+------------------------------------------+
| Instance         | Data unique to each object               |
| Static           | Shared data/utility methods              |
| public           | API, meant to be used everywhere         |
| private          | Internal implementation details          |
| protected        | For derived classes only                 |
| Auto-property    | Simple get/set without logic             |
| Computed         | Calculate value on-the-fly               |
| Inheritance      | "is-a" relationship, code reuse          |
| Interface        | Contract, multiple inheritance           |
| Abstract         | Partial implementation, template         |
+------------------+------------------------------------------+
```
